title: Development and External Validation of an Updated Nomogram Including Both MRI and Local PSMA PET/CT Information for the Prediction of Side-specific Extraprostatic Extension in Patients Treated with Radical Prostatectomy

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Development and External Validation of an Updated Nomogram Including Both MRI and Local PSMA PET/CT Information for the Prediction of Side-specific Extraprostatic Extension in Patients Treated with Radical Prostatectomy》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0055】This study aimed to develop and externally validate a side-specific prediction model for EPE incorporating PSMA PET/CT-derived variables alongside MRI and clinical parameters, and to evaluate its performance, in terms of discrimination, calibration, and net benefit, in comparison with an existing MRI-based model (Soeterik).

【Objective · abstract-2-1】We assessed whether adding PSMA PET/CT to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical factors improves side-specific EPE prediction.

evidence.text: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a side-specific prediction model for EPE incorporating PSMA PET/CT-derived variables alongside MRI and clinical parameters, and to evaluate its performance, in terms of discrimination, calibration, and net benefit, in comparison with an existing MRI-based model (Soeterik).
We assessed whether adding PSMA PET/CT to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical factors improves side-specific EPE prediction.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Development and External Validation of an Updated Nomogram Including Both MRI and Local PSMA PET/CT Information for the Prediction of Side-specific Extraprostatic Extension in Patients Treated with Radical Prostatectomy》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patient population and study data · p0060】The patient population was derived from a previously published multicentre cohort of men who underwent RP, with or without pelvic lymph node dissection, at seven tertiary referral centres and who were preoperatively staged with PSMA PET/CT between May 2016, when PSMA PET/CT became available for preoperative staging, and June 2023 [21] (Supplementary File 1). Patients were required to be treatment naive at the time of imaging. The indication for preoperative PSMA PET/CT was determined by the local multidisciplinary team, reflecting real-world practice. Because PSMA PET/CT was introduced at different time points across centres, the contributing period varied per centre. At two centres, patients enrolled in the prospective PSMA Select trial [22] were managed within that trial and were not included in the present retrospective cohort; apart from this, consecutive patients were included at all centres.

【Patient population and study data · p0065】Of the 605 patients in this cohort, 48 were excluded because no presurgical MRI was available, leaving 557 patients. The cohort was subsequently divided by centre into a validation cohort (centre 1; n = 146) and a development cohort (remaining centres; n = 411). Because the prediction model is side specific, all analyses were performed at the level of the prostatic lobe. Lobes with missing data for any of the model variables (Standardized Uptake Value max (SUVmax), PSMAtotal, PSAD, or MRI T-stage) were excluded at this stage. This resulted in 801 lobes from 401 patients in the development cohort and 287 lobes from 144 patients in the validation cohort. The full selection process, including the number of patients excluded at each step, is now presented in a flow diagram (Supplementary File 2A). The institutional review boards approved the study prior to initiating data collection (AW24.048/W18.055). Written informed consent was waived because of the retrospective nature of the study.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Development and External Validation of an Updated Nomogram Including Both MRI and Local PSMA PET/CT Information for the Prediction of Side-specific Extraprostatic Extension in Patients Treated with Radical Prostatectomy》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Model performance, external validation, and clinical usefulness · p0110】Model discrimination, defined as the ability of the model to distinguish a prostate lobe with EPE from a lobe without EPE, was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) [34]. The AUC ranges between 0.5 and 1, with higher values indicating better discrimination between patients with the endpoint and without the endpoint [35]. Model calibration, reflecting the agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes, was evaluated using calibration-in-the-large (systematic overprediction or underprediction) and calibration slope [34]. The net benefit per risk threshold was determined using decision-curve analysis (DCA). Net benefit, assessed across risk thresholds of 0–50%, reflects the number of true positives gained by using the model, after adjusting for false positives at each threshold [36]. Therefore, the 0–50% range reflects probability levels at which imaging-derived information meaningfully contributes to postimaging risk stratification, before definitive therapeutic decisions, such as surgical planning, are made by the urologist or multidisciplinary team. The original MRI-based nomogram (Soeterik model 2) was applied using its published coefficients, without refitting, in both the development and the validation cohort [13]. Discrimination, calibration, and net benefit were assessed for both nomograms in each cohort, allowing direct comparison of performance within the same populations. DeLong test was used to assess statistically significant differences in AUCs between models. Effect modification by PSMA tracer type was assessed by adding interaction terms between tracer type and all covariates and testing the full interaction block with a Wald test. For statistical analysis, R version 4.4.0 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Vienna, Austria) was used.

【Model performance of the updated PSMA-MRI combined nomogram in the development cohort and comparison with the original MRI-based nomogram · p0130】In the development cohort, adding the PSMA-derived predictors to a model containing the same clinical and MRI predictors, refitted in the present cohort, statistically significantly improved model fit (Wald c2 = 32.1, p < 0.001), with a modest accompanying gain in discrimination (AUC 0.78 [95% CI 0.75–0.81] to 0.80 [95% CI 0.77–0.83]). Calibration of the previously developed MRI-based nomogram was externally validated in the development cohort using its original published coefficients. It showed an AUC of 0.77 (95% CI 0.73–0.80). Calibration deviated from ideal, with a slope of 0.81 (95% CI 0.68–0.95) and an intercept of 0.24 (95% CI 0.07–0.41), indicating somewhat too extreme predictions together with a systematic underestimation of the observed EPE risk (Fig. 2A). Adding interactions between tracer type and all covariates improved model fit (Wald c2 = 23.5, degrees of freedom = 10, p = 0.009), driven predominantly by MRI T-stage, with no interaction for PSAD, PSMAtotal, or PSMA T-stage. Because the tracer type was fully confounded with the centre, the interaction terms were not retained in the final model. Model performance per tracer is shown descriptively in Supplementary File 9.
